claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr material is a random solid solution.
The random HfNbTaTiZr solid solution has high configurational entropy.
Atomic-size mismatch causes significant local lattice distortion in the random HfNbTaTiZr solid solution.
Chemical short-range ordering produces HfTi and TiZr binary clusters with local B2-like order.
The B2-like HfTi and TiZr clusters can form a percolating network.
The percolating B2-like clusters locally relax lattice strain.
Interfaces between the ordered clusters and matrix are coherent and have reduced phonon-scattering cross-sections.
Ordering reduces local lattice distortion more strongly than it adds scattering from cluster interfaces.
Reduced lattice distortion lowers the scattering potential and scattering rates of high-frequency phonons.
Formation of the ordered clusters shifts the high-frequency phonon DOS to lower frequencies.
The lower-frequency states created by the DOS shift have higher phonon group velocities.
Percolating networks of ordered clusters provide pathways that facilitate ballistic phonon transport.
Percolating SRO increases lattice thermal conductivity relative to the random HfNbTaTiZr solid solution.
Atomic displacement amplitudes within the ordered clusters are lower than in the random state.
The random solid solution has low thermal conductivity because random lattice distortion and mass variance strongly scatter phonons.
Below the SRO-cluster percolation threshold, the alloy remains disorder-dominated and does not exhibit the proposed conductivity increase.
If ordered clusters grow into large precipitates with incoherent interfaces, interface scattering dominates and thermal conductivity decreases.
The proposed effect occurs where SRO is thermodynamically stable and the phonon mean free path is comparable to the cluster spacing.
